function_review.how_the_model_runs:
The model does not predict. Each time a sensor value changes, it recalculates every function once, in step order (1, 2, 3a, 3b, 3c, 3d, 4, 5, 6), as an algebraic steady-state chain with no time step (behaviour_solver type="algebraic_chain").
Each computed value has two parts: X' from the function below, plus X'' from the feedback loop (coupling type="additive"). The feedback loop may write only onto computed (PRELIMINARY) attributes. It never changes a measured (SENSOR) input.
Every value_at_baseline below is X' alone: all 11 inputs at their declared baseline, with no feedback correction applied.

attribute.name: Systolic Blood Pressure
attribute.wearable: no: needs a cuff (cuff readings can be stored in Apple Health)

attribute.name: Diastolic Blood Pressure
attribute.wearable: no: needs a cuff (cuff readings can be stored in Apple Health)

attribute.name: Vessel Length
attribute.wearable: no: one representative segment, not a measurable quantity

function.name: Pressure Regulation
function.description: Computes mean arterial pressure. DBP weighted 2/3 because diastole is ~2x longer than systole.

function.name: Vascular Resistance
function.description: Poiseuille's Law for a single rigid cylindrical segment. r^4 dependence: 50% radius reduction = 16x resistance increase. Assumes steady laminar Newtonian flow in one rigid tube — it is a representative estimate, not whole-body SVR.
function.implementation_note: The formula is evaluated in CGS units (dyne.s/cm^5) and converted to mmHg.min/L by multiplying by 60 / (1333.22 * 1000). eta enters the formula as declared, without converting mPa.s to poise. See open point 1.

function.name: Cardiac Filling
function.description: Frank-Starling Law. Heart pumps what it receives, capped at physiological limit.
function.implementation_note: SV = k * min(EDV, EDV_limit), with k = 0.55 and EDV_limit = 200 mL. Both constants are in the Python class, not in the XML. The code also holds two alternative profiles, heart failure (k = 0.30, limit = 150 mL) and athletic (k = 0.65, limit = 220 mL), but nothing in the application selects them. See open point 3.

function.name: Cardiac Pump
function.description: Primary pump output. HR from Apple Watch, SV from cardiac_filling.

function.name: Cardiac Rhythm
function.description: Cycle length from rate. Arithmetically trivial, but it is what lets a consumer read rhythm as a model output instead of reaching for the HR sensor — the model carries the complexity, the consumer reads a result.
function.implementation_note: Matches the formula. Raises an error if HR is not positive.

function.name: Systolic Interval
function.description: Weissler's regression for left ventricular ejection time (seconds, adult male resting cohort). Replaces a fixed systolic fraction: ejection time falls with rate far more slowly than cycle length does, so systole takes up a larger share of a fast cycle. Coefficients are population regression, not per-patient — worth recalibrating against a real cohort before clinical claims.
function.implementation_note: Floored at 0.05 s. Within the declared HR range (up to 200 bpm) the floor is never reached. See open point 4.

function.name: Hemodynamic Flow
function.description: Ohm's Law for hemodynamics. Driving pressure is the arterio-venous gradient (MAP - CVP), not MAP alone; CVP was a Python constant and is now a declared SENSOR attribute (baseline 5 mmHg) a domain expert can edit. NOTE: R here is a single-segment Poiseuille estimate, so Q's ABSOLUTE value is unreliable; trust its trend, not its magnitude (see R).
function.implementation_note: Matches the formula. Raises an error if R is not positive. See open point 2.

function.name: Electrical Conduction
function.description: Cable Theory length constant lambda = sqrt(r_m / (r_i + r_e)). Relates to passive conduction (a longer lambda spreads charge further); the link to P-wave / arrhythmia risk is indirect and should be treated as illustrative, not diagnostic.
function.implementation_note: Matches the formula. No other function reads lambda. See open point 5.

function.name: Systemic Vascular Resistance
function.description: Derived whole-body resistance from what the twin already measures: MAP from the SBP/DBP cuff, CO from the HR and EDV sensors, CVP from the declared CVP sensor. Dividing the arterio-venous gradient by the pump's output gives the resistance the pressure branch was missing — R (step 2) is a single-segment Poiseuille estimate that cannot move with the pump, so it can never reconcile Q with CO; SVR can.
function.implementation_note: Matches the formula. Raises an error if CO is zero or negative, or if any input is missing or not finite.

dependency_chain.branch: eta, L, r -> R ; MAP, R, CVP -> Q
r_m, r_i, r_e -> lambda (standalone, not connected to the other branches)

open_points.point: Units of eta. eta is declared in mPa.s but enters the CGS formula unconverted. Since 1 mPa.s = 0.01 poise, R comes out 100 times larger than with consistent units. At baseline: R = 39.62 mmHg.min/L as computed, against 0.40 mmHg.min/L with eta in poise. The computed value sits at the top of R's declared range (10 to 40). The description of R says it is "calibrated" to land in the systemic range, and this factor of 100 is where that calibration comes from. Question: keep it as an explicit, declared calibration factor, or drop R in favour of SVR (step 6)?

Q and CO disagree. Both are a flow in L/min, but at baseline Q = 2.23 while CO = 4.75, a difference of about 2x, because Q divides by the single-segment R. SVR (step 6) was added to give a resistance that moves with the pump. Question: should Q and R stay in the model for their trend only, or be disabled?

The Frank-Starling constants k = 0.55 and EDV_limit = 200 mL are hidden in Python, so they cannot be reviewed or changed in the XML. For an athlete twin, the existing "athletic" profile (k = 0.65, limit = 220 mL) is relevant but currently unused. Proposal: move k and EDV_limit into the XML as declared parameters.

Weissler's regression was fitted on resting subjects. Used together with T_cycle, it gives a systolic fraction (T_sys / T_cycle) that rises with HR only up to about 120 bpm and then falls again: 0.27 at 50 bpm, 0.35 at 72, 0.42 at 120, 0.35 at 170, 0.29 at 190 bpm. Physiologically, systole takes a larger share of the cycle as HR rises, which is also what the function's own description says. Exercise heart rates in athletes (150 to 190 bpm) fall in the range where the extrapolated regression reverses. Question: is another LVET relation valid at exercise heart rates, or should HR be capped for this function?

Units of lambda. With r_m in ohm.cm and r_i, r_e in ohm/cm, sqrt(r_m / (r_i + r_e)) has units of cm, but the output is labelled mm. Read as cm, the baseline 3.16 is 31.6 mm, outside the declared range of 0.5 to 5 mm. lambda also feeds no other function. Question: correct the unit, or disable this branch for the athlete level 1?

Wearable coverage for the athlete level 1. Of the 11 inputs, only HR comes from a consumer wearable, and SBP/DBP come from a cuff. As a result: - T_cycle and T_sys are fully driven by wearable data. - MAP needs a cuff. - SV and CO need EDV, which no wearable measures, so EDV must be held at a declared value or estimated by the model. - SVR needs MAP, CO and CVP. - R, Q and lambda need inputs that no wearable provides. Question: for each input that is not measured, should it be disabled, held at its declared baseline (and shown as assumed), or estimated through the feedback loop?
